title: The sergeant's colic
note: Floyd wrote on 31 July 1804, at this camp: 'I am verry Sick and has been for Somtime but have Recovered my helth again'. He had not; on 19 August he was taken very bad with what Clark called a bilious colic, and he died the next day, almost certainly of a burst appendix. Nothing here changes that (ADR-0012). What the captain decides is how the Corps meets it, with the physic of 1804: Rush's purging pills, the lancet, rest.

lines.speaker: Sgt. Floyd
lines.text: I've been very sick for some time, Captain. But I believe I've recovered my health again.

lines.speaker: York
lines.text: He's eaten nothing since yesterday, Captain Lewis.

choices.label: Dose him with Rush's pills
choices.note: Calomel and jalap. The men call them thunderbolts. They purge a man hard.

reply.speaker: Sgt. Floyd
reply.text: Thunderbolts. Well, sir. If you think it best.

choices.label: Bleed him
choices.note: The physic of the age: let the fever out with the blood.

effects.journal: Sergeant Floyd bled, for the colic.

reply.speaker: Sgt. Floyd
reply.text: I'm obliged to you, Captain. I feel lighter for it.

choices.label: Excuse him from duty; let him lie in the boat

effects.journal: Sergeant Floyd excused from duty, and lies in the boat out of the sun.

reply.speaker: Sgt. Floyd
reply.text: Pryor will see to my mess, sir. It's only for the day.

choices.label: Take him at his word
choices.note: He says he is mending, and a sergeant wants to be seen at his duty.

effects.journal: Sergeant Floyd says he is mended, and keeps to his duty.

lines.speaker: Clark
lines.text: Keep an eye on him, Sergeant Pryor.
